title: Triple-Difference Estimators
text: triplediff R package computing average treatment effects Triple Differences Designs (also known Difference--Differences--Differences DDD). DDD designs widely used empirical work relax parallel trends assumptions Difference--Differences settings. package provides functions estimate group-time average treatment effect event-study type estimands associated DDD designs. setups allowed : Two-periods Multiple Periods DDD. Single Treatment Date Variation Treatment Timing (.e., staggered adoption). Conditional Unconditional DDD parallel trends assumptions. triplediff package implements framework proposed : Ortiz-Villavicencio, Marcelo Pedro H.C. Sant’Anna. “Better Understanding Triple Differences Estimators”, 2025.

title: Triple-Difference Estimators
text: provide quick start example illustrate main features package. UX designed similar package, users familiar feel comfortable using triplediff. ddd main function computing DDD estimators proposed Ortiz-Villavicencio Sant’Anna (2025). core, ddd employs regression adjustment, inverse probability weighting, doubly robust estimators valid conditional DDD parallel trends. use ddd, minimal data requirements include: id: Unit unique identifier (e.g., firm, individual, etc.). column name associated parameter idname. period: Time identifier (e.g., year, month, etc.). column name associated parameter tname. outcome: Outcome variable interest. column name associated parameter yname. state: First period treatment enabled particular unit. positive number treated units defines group unit belongs . takes value 0 Inf never-enabling units. column name associated parameter gname. partition: indicator variable 1 units eligible treatment 0 otherwise. column name associated parameter pname. , S period unit’s group enables treatment (gname column), Q eligibility (pname column). unit treated period t t ≥ S Q = 1. group S = 0 Inf never enables treatment. write S = ∞. following two simplified examples use ddd function. first one multiple-period DDD setup staggered treatment adoption. goes raw data event study. second one two-period DDD setup.

what: Multiple periods with staggered adoption: from the data to an event study
title: Triple-Difference Estimators
text: First, can simulate data built-function gen_dgp_mult_periods generates multiple-period DDD setup staggered treatment adoption. function receives number units type DGP design generate. gen_dgp_mult_periods function returns data frame required columns ddd function 4 covariates. Step 1: look data. unit belongs one six groups: enabling period S (2, 3 ∞) eligibility Q (1 0). heatmap draws one row per unit one column per period. eligible units group enabled treatment treated.  DDD compares treated cells three comparison groups. ATT(2,2) control_group = "nevertreated", ineligible units S = 2 group, eligible ineligible units S = ∞ group. Step 2: estimate group-time effects. Now can estimate group-time average treatment effect treated using ddd function. plot() draws ATT(g,t) confidence interval. Pre-treatment cells gold, post-treatment cells dark blue.  Step 3: aggregate event study. , can aggregate group-time average treatment effect treated obtain event-study type estimates. agg_ddd function allows us aggregate results ddd function. plot() draws event study. returns ggplot object, can change +.
code: set.seed(1234) # Set seed for reproducibility # Simulate data for a multiple-period DDD setup with staggered treatment adoption data <- gen_dgp_mult_periods(size = 500, dgp_type = 1)$data  head(data) #> Key: <id> #>       id state partition  time         y        cov1       cov2       cov3 #>    <int> <num>     <num> <int>     <num>       <num>      <num>      <num> #> 1:     1     3         1     1 1371.1923 -0.97080934  1.3995704 1.48834130 #> 2:     1     3         1     2 1690.9157 -0.97080934  1.3995704 1.48834130 #> 3:     1     3         1     3 2034.5661 -0.97080934  1.3995704 1.48834130 #> 4:     2     2         1     1  934.0812  0.02591115 -0.9747527 0.01714001 #> 5:     2     2         1     2 1189.5495  0.02591115 -0.9747527 0.01714001 #> 6:     2     2         1     3 1444.1072  0.02591115 -0.9747527 0.01714001 #>          cov4 cluster #>         <num>   <int> #> 1:  0.3853346      27 #> 2:  0.3853346      27 #> 3:  0.3853346      27 #> 4: -0.7822000      45 #> 5: -0.7822000      45 #> 6: -0.7822000      45 library(ggplot2)  # Status of each unit in each period. S is the enabling period (`state`, # 0 = never), Q is eligibility (`partition`), t is the period (`time`). status_of <- function(S, Q, t) {   enabled <- S != 0 & t >= S   ifelse(enabled & Q == 1, "Treated: enabled and eligible",   ifelse(enabled,          "Enabled, not eligible",   ifelse(S != 0 & Q == 1,  "Eligible, enabled later", "Not enabled"))) } status_colors <- c("Treated: enabled and eligible" = "#154780",                    "Eligible, enabled later"       = "#B3CBE6",                    "Enabled, not eligible"         = "#B28C1C",                    "Not enabled"                   = "#E3E9E5")  units <- unique(as.data.frame(data)[, c("id", "state", "partition")]) units <- units[order(match(units$state, c(2, 3, 0)), -units$partition, units$id), ] block <- paste(match(units$state, c(2, 3, 0)), 1 - units$partition)  # one block per (S, Q) units$row <- seq_len(nrow(units)) + 8 * (match(block, unique(block)) - 1)  # gaps between blocks  cells <- merge(as.data.frame(data), units[, c("id", "row")], by = "id") cells$status <- factor(status_of(cells$state, cells$partition, cells$time),                        levels = names(status_colors)) labels <- aggregate(row ~ state + partition, data = units,                     FUN = function(r) c(mid = mean(r), n = length(r))) labels <- data.frame(labels[1:2], labels$row) labels$text <- sprintf("S = %s, Q = %d (%d units)",                        ifelse(labels$state == 0, "∞", labels$state),                        labels$partition, labels$n)  p_heat <- ggplot(cells, aes(x = time, y = row, fill = status)) +   geom_tile(width = 0.97, height = 1) +   scale_fill_manual(values = status_colors, drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +   scale_y_reverse(breaks = labels$mid, labels = labels$text, expand = c(0.01, 0)) +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:3, labels = paste("t =", 1:3), expand = c(0, 0)) +   labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,        title = "Who is treated, and when",        subtitle = "One row per unit, grouped by enabling period S and eligibility Q") +   theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +   theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",         plot.title.position = "plot") +   guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)) # Estimate the group-time average treatment effect in DDD  att_gt <- ddd(yname = "y", tname = "time", idname = "id", gname = "state",                pname = "partition", xformla = ~cov1 + cov2 + cov3 + cov4,               data = data, control_group = "nevertreated",                base_period = "universal", est_method = "dr")  summary(att_gt) #>  Call: #> ddd(yname = "y", tname = "time", idname = "id", gname = "state",  #>     pname = "partition", xformla = ~cov1 + cov2 + cov3 + cov4,  #>     data = data, control_group = "nevertreated", base_period = "universal",  #>     est_method = "dr") #> =========================== DDD Summary ============================== #>  DR-DDD estimation for the ATT(g,t):  #> Group Time  ATT(g,t)  Std. Error [95% Pointwise  Conf. Band]   #>   2    1       0.0000         NA           NA            NA    #>   2    2      10.4901     0.3613       9.7819       11.1983  * #>   2    3      20.5986     0.3868      19.8405       21.3568  * #>   3    1      -0.4593     0.3660      -1.1767        0.2580    #>   3    2       0.0000         NA           NA            NA    #>   3    3      24.5983     0.3333      23.9450       25.2515  * #>  #>  Note: * indicates that the confidence interval does not contain zero. #>  --------------------------- Data Info   ----------------------------- #>  Panel Data #>  Outcome variable: y #>  Qualification variable: partition #>  Control group: Never Treated #>  No. of units per treatment group: #>   Units enabling treatment at period 3: 198 #>   Units enabling treatment at period 2: 195 #>   Units never enabling treatment: 107 #>  --------------------------- Algorithms ------------------------------ #>  Outcome Regression estimated using: OLS #>  Propensity score estimated using: Maximum Likelihood #>  --------------------------- Std. Errors  ---------------------------- #>  Level of significance:  0.05 #>  Analytical standard errors. #>  Type of confidence band:  Pointwise Confidence Interval #>  ===================================================================== #>  See Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna (2025) for details. plot(att_gt) es_e <- agg_ddd(att_gt, type = "eventstudy")  summary(es_e) #>  Call: #> agg_ddd(ddd_obj = att_gt, type = "eventstudy") #> ========================= DDD Aggregation ============================ #>  Overall summary of ATT's based on event-study/dynamic aggregation:  #>     ATT    Std. Error     [ 95%  Conf. Int.]   #>  19.398        0.3564    18.6994     20.0965 * #>  #>  Event Study: #>  Event time Estimate Std. Error [95% Ptwise.  Conf. Band]   #>          -2  -0.4593     0.3660       -1.1767      0.2580   #>          -1   0.0000         NA            NA          NA   #>           0  18.1973     0.5179       17.1823     19.2123 * #>           1  20.5986     0.3868       19.8405     21.3568 * #>  #>  Note: * indicates that the confidence interval does not contain zero. #>  --------------------------- Data Info   ----------------------------- #>  Outcome variable: y #>  Qualification variable: partition #>  Control group:  Never Treated #>  --------------------------- Std. Errors  ---------------------------- #>  Level of significance:  0.05 #>  Analytical standard errors. #>  ===================================================================== #>  See Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna (2025) for details. plot(es_e)

title: Triple-Difference Estimators
text: gruber1994 holds data Gruber (1994), classic DDD application. Three states (IL, NJ NY) passed laws required health insurance cover maternity. laws took effect July 1976 January 1977, treatment_starts 1976 states. eligible group (Q = 1) married women aged 20 40. data repeated cross-sections: row different worker. heatmap counts workers state, group year.  Reference: Gruber, J. (1994). Incidence Mandated Maternity Benefits. American Economic Review, 84(3), 622-641.
code:
cells_g <- aggregate(id ~ state + treat_group + year + treatment_starts,                      data = gruber1994, FUN = length) names(cells_g)[names(cells_g) == "id"] <- "workers" cells_g$status <- factor(status_of(cells_g$treatment_starts, cells_g$treat_group, cells_g$year),                          levels = names(status_colors)) cells_g$group <- factor(ifelse(cells_g$treatment_starts == 0,                                "Comparison states
(never enable)",                                "Mandate states
(enable in 1976)"),                         levels = c("Mandate states
(enable in 1976)",                                    "Comparison states
(never enable)")) cells_g <- cells_g[order(cells_g$group, cells_g$state, -cells_g$treat_group), ] cells_g$row <- paste0(cells_g$state, ", Q = ", cells_g$treat_group) cells_g$row <- factor(cells_g$row, levels = rev(unique(cells_g$row)))  # The counts are dark on every cell except the Treated cells, where they are white. p_gruber <- ggplot(cells_g, aes(x = factor(year), y = row, fill = status)) +   geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +   geom_text(aes(label = workers,                 colour = status != "Treated: enabled and eligible"),             size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#1E2B27", `FALSE` = "white")) +   scale_fill_manual(values = status_colors, drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +   facet_grid(rows = vars(group), scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +   labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Gruber (1994): workers per state, group and year",        subtitle = "Q = 1: married women aged 20 to 40. Mandates took effect from July 1976 to January 1977.") +   theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +   theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",         strip.placement = "outside", strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0),         plot.title.position = "plot") +   guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))

title: Aggregate Group-Time Average Treatment Effects in Staggered Triple-Differences Designs. — agg_ddd
text: agg_ddd function take group-time average treatment effects aggregate smaller number summary parameters staggered triple differences designs. several possible aggregations including "simple", "eventstudy", "group", "calendar".  Default "eventstudy".

title: Aggregate Group-Time Average Treatment Effects in Staggered Triple-Differences Designs. — agg_ddd
code: agg_ddd(   ddd_obj,   type = "eventstudy",   cluster = NULL,   balance_e = NULL,   min_e = -Inf,   max_e = Inf,   na.rm = FALSE,   boot = NULL,   nboot = NULL,   cband = NULL,   alpha = NULL )

title: Aggregate Group-Time Average Treatment Effects in Staggered Triple-Differences Designs. — agg_ddd
text: ddd_obj ddd object (.e., results ddd() function) type type aggregated treatment effect parameter compute. "simple" computes weighted average post-treatment group-time average treatment effects, cohort weights proportional share treated units cohort. "eventstudy" computes average effects across different lengths exposure treatment (event times). overall effect averages effect treatment across positive lengths exposure. default option; "group" computes average treatment effects across different groups/cohorts; overall effect averages effect across different groups, weights proportional share treated units cohort; "calendar" computes average treatment effects across different time periods, cohort weights proportional share treated units; overall effect averages effect across time period. See Details cohort weights. cluster name variable used clustering. maximum number cluster variables 1. Default NULL. balance_e set (one computes event study), balances sample respect event time.  example, balance_e=2, agg_ddd drop groups exposed treatment least three periods, initial period e=0 well next two periods, e=1 e=2.  ensures composition groups change event time changes. min_e event studies, smallest event time compute dynamic effects .  default, min_e = -Inf effects lengths exposure computed. max_e event studies, largest event time compute dynamic effects .  default, max_e = Inf effects lengths exposure computed. na.rm Logical value remove missing Values analyses. Defaults FALSE. boot Boolean whether compute standard errors using multiplier bootstrap.  standard errors clustered, one must set boot=TRUE. Default value set ddd object.  boot = FALSE, analytical standard errors reported. nboot number bootstrap iterations use.  default value set ddd object, applicable boot=TRUE. cband Boolean whether compute uniform confidence band covers aggregated treatment effects fixed probability 1 - alpha.  order compute uniform confidence bands, boot must also set TRUE.  default value set ddd object. alpha significance level confidence intervals bands. default, NULL, uses level stored ddd object (alpha passed ddd()).

title: triplediff 0.2.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-01-16 Replaced parglm fastglm avoid issues related parglm’s scheduled archival 2026-01-29. Added support unbalanced panel data repeated cross-sectional data properly implementing allow_unbalanced_panel parameter across functions.

title: triplediff 0.2.1
text: Add asymmetric propensity score trimming control units pscore >= 0.995. Add partition-specific collinearity detection two-stage checking. Add comprehensive test suite including Monte Carlo coverage test trimming.

title: triplediff 0.2.2
text: Track BMisc (>= 1.4.9) API rename: replaced makeBalancedPanel make_balanced_panel rhs.vars rhs_vars internal preprocessing. user-visible behavior change. (#34) Replaced remaining deprecated BMisc::getListElement call BMisc::get_list_element silence deprecation warnings (follow-#34).

title: triplediff 0.2.3
text: Added analytical cluster-robust standard errors without bootstrap multiple-period path. Calling ddd() cluster = <var> boot = FALSE now returns analytical cluster-robust standard errors (cluster-sum CRVE influence function) instead requiring bootstrap. ddd object now carries cluster_vector cluster_var. Two-period designs still require boot = TRUE clustered inference. Added cluster argument agg_ddd(). Aggregated parameters (simple, event-study, group, calendar) now report analytical cluster-robust standard errors. clustering requested different variable ddd() used (object built without clustering), agg_ddd() warns falls back ..d. standard errors instead silently mis-reporting. Behavior change: clustered multiplier bootstrap now follows Callaway & Sant’Anna (2021, Remark 10), applying one multiplier per cluster influence function aggregated cluster sums rather cluster means. Clustered bootstrap standard errors change unbalanced clusters repeated cross-sections; equal-sized clusters unaffected.

title: triplediff 0.2.4
text: CRAN release: 2026-06-13 Resubmission. Simplified ddd() examples removing bootstrap-based clustered standard errors example, package examples stay within CRAN’s limit number cores used checks. changes package functionality.

text: Added gruber1994 dataset Gruber (1994) maternity-mandate data. See ?gruber1994. Added plot() methods ddd agg_ddd objects return ggplot object (requires ggplot2). See ?plot.ddd ?plot.agg_ddd.

Fixed standard errors GMM cells control_group = "notyettreated" balanced panels. point estimates cells aggregates use also move slightly.
